newsitem.title: INDIA: Japan's Marubeni marks $100 mln for India.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Marubeni marks $100 mln for India.

text.p: Japan's Marubeni Corp plans to to invest $100 million in India by 2000, a senior company official said on Monday.

"We are planning to invest about $100 million by 2000 in textiles, metals, chemicals and machinery. We are also considering a leasing company," said T. Mori, manager of Marubeni India Pvt Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Marubeni Corp.

Mori, speaking to Reuters at the 12th Indian Engineering Trade Fair, said the firm was in the process of finalising a joint venture with Japan's Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd and an Indian partner to manufacture light passenger cars in India.
He said Marubeni would be a minority shareholder in the venture, but gave no other details. He did not name the Indian company.
He said another joint venture to make engines for tractors and other farm vehicles was also under consideration.
Mori said Marubeni planned to set up a factory to make aluminium products and a turn-key petrochemicals project over the next three years.
Marubeni India's assistant general manager, T. Yoshida, said the firm planned to build up to four integrated garment manufacture units in India over the next three years.

The factories would entail investment of up to $2 billion, but Marubeni would contribute only an unspecified part of that amount, Yoshida said. The rest would be brought in by an Indian partner, he said.
"We have decided on a partner and we are negotiating terms, including an equity stake," Yoshida said. He gave no other details.
